# yahara

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

Multiverse analysis is a technique to assess the reproducibility of scientific findings by assessing how much they vary when reasonable alternative choices are made in data processing and modeling. 
Visualizing this variation assists in interpreting a multiverse analysis, but doing so when there are multiple estimands (a target quantity, such as a coefficient, test statistic, or p-value) of interest is challenging. Each estimand has its own distribution to visualize, and each multiverse decision could affect multiple estimands. Popular existing methods only focus on a single estimand at a time, and iterating over estimands with them would miss correlations across estimands, and would become impractical as the number of estimands increases. 

To address this gap, we introduce the R package Yahara. Yahara presents an interactive Shiny interface of linked panels that enables efficient identification of the most variable estimands and most impactful options in multiverse analyses with multiple estimands, as well as more focused visualization of estimands, universes, and effects of interest.

## Installation

You can install the development version of yahara from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("cjones46/yahara")
```

## Example

``` r
# library(yahara)
# yahara(SusiesMultiverse, "summary_fit")
```
